newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU rejects textile aid, but open to talks.
newsitem.headline: EU rejects textile aid, but open to talks.

text.p: The European Commission said on Wednesday it had banned a French state aid scheme targeted at the textiles and clothing industries, but said it was open to discussions about a plan that would apply more widely.

EU Competition Commissioner Karel Van Miert has invited French authorities to discuss ways of broadening or widening the system, for example to cover all sectors that are heavily dependent on manual labour, it said in a statement.
"(The Commission) does not find fault with the plan's aims of job creation but rather with the fact that it supports certain sectors only," the European Union executive said in a statement.

The French plan, which has been allocated a budget of 2.1 billion French francs ($365.2 billion) per year for a period of 18 months, grants aid to employers in the form of cuts or exemptions in their social security contributions for low-paid workers.
The Commission said the French plan did not create problems for some 11,300 of the 13,000 firms concerned since the benefits they received did not exceed minimum thresholds for state aid.
"On the other hand, the Commission's decision requires the aid to be recovered in cases where that threshold is exceeded," the Commission said.
